reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant classification (retained as internal evidence, not a negotiation issue).

The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 11.1(a) leaves Ono (our party) owning IP created solely by its personnel, 11.1(b) only preserves Array's own solely-created IP (expressly acceptable under the rule: 'Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine'), and no paragraph assigns our IP, know-how or data to Array. The Section 2.6 grant-back is a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence limited to the Products and expressly subject to Ono's exclusive rights — a licence, not an assignment, so it is not walk-away territory.

Directionally favourable terms are correctly not flagged: Array must assign registered Product Trademarks in the Ono Territory to us (12.2) and we own Marketing Approvals/regulatory submissions in our Territory (p0329) — flagging these would be over-flagging against our own interest.

The joint-ownership point in 11.1(c)-(d) is properly noted rather than redlined: Joint Inventions are defined as relating to Binimetinib/Encorafenib/Products, and the (d) restriction is expressly disapplied for subject matter licensed between the Parties, so within the deal scope we retain exploitation rights via the exclusive licences — this is not 'joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit', and the restriction is symmetric.

Rationale is accurate against the supplied paragraphs and appropriately explains the residual, non-material shortfalls (term/territory-limited rather than perpetual licences, domain-name reversion) as characteristics of a territorial in-licence rather than deviations; the deterministic check (no assignment of our IP/data to Vendor) also passes.
